notes.text: A flaw was found in go-git, an extensible Git implementation library. Worktree operations, such as checkout, status, and add, resolve symbolic links within the working tree without proper boundary confinement. This allows a remote attacker to craft a malicious repository containing a symlink, which, when cloned and its worktree operations are used, can lead to reading from or writing to arbitrary files outside the intended working directory. This could result in information disclosure or arbitrary file modification.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/go-git/go-git/v5: go-git: Arbitrary file read/write via symbolic link resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: go-git is a pure-Go implementation of Git. During worktree operations (checkout, status, add), go-git resolves symbolic links without confining resolution to the worktree boundary, so a maliciously crafted repository containing a symlink can cause a consuming application to read from or write to files outside the intended working directory when that repository is cloned and its worktree operations are used. Exploitation requires the application to clone an attacker-controlled repository and then perform worktree operations against it; applications that only process trusted repositories are not exposed. Red Hat rates the impact of this flaw as Important.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a software component used for parsing Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) in Node.js applications. This vulnerability arises from an issue in how fast-uri processes the scheme part of a URI, specifically when it contains special characters that are percent-encoded. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious URI, causing the parser to misinterpret the host, which can lead to serious security risks. These risks include unauthorized redirection to external websites, server-side request forgery (SSRF) where the application makes unintended requests to internal or external resources, and bypassing security policies.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: URI parsing flaw enables server-side request forgery and redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A host confusion vulnerability was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. The parser runs a legacy decoding pass over the scheme component and never re-escapes the result. As a consequence, an input whose scheme carries percent-encoded slashes parses as having no authority (undefined host), yet resolving or normalizing that same input emits a network-path reference with an attacker-chosen authority. Applications that normalize or resolve untrusted URLs before a redirect check, host allowlist, or outbound request decision can be steered to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF), open redirect, or address-policy bypass. Additionally, a normalized URI in a response header can carry injected carriage return line feed (CRLF) characters, enabling HTTP response splitting attacks such as cache poisoning or session hijacking. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: GitPython before 3.1.59 fails to safely re-serialize multi-line git-config values during write operations, corrupting dormant quoted values into injected directives like core.hooksPath. notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: gitpython: GitPython before 3.1.59 Remote Code Execution via Config Injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
Case for AC:H (8.1): the trigger needs two things the attacker does not
  straightforwardly own:
    (1) a crafted multi-line quoted value must already sit DORMANT in .git/config
        — the guarded set_value() path will not put it there; it must arrive via
        _read() of a file the attacker influenced but does not directly write; and
    (2) a SUBSEQUENT, UNRELATED GitPython config WRITE must fire to re-serialize
        and corrupt it — and that write is performed by the victim application on
        its own schedule, not by the attacker. 
    "Prepare the target environment" + "conditions beyond the attacker's control"
    is the textbook AC:H definition; step (2) in particular fits it.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to create arbitrary Git directories outside the intended clone destination. By manipulating the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning, an attacker can redirect repository metadata to an attacker-controlled filesystem path. This could lead to arbitrary directory creation and potentially enable the execution of malicious code through Git hooks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: GitPython: GitPython: Arbitrary Code Execution via Path Traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has identified a path traversal vulnerability in GitPython versions before 3.1.59. The vulnerability arises because the `--separate-git-dir` option is not included in the `unsafe_git_clone_options` denylist, allowing attackers who control the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning to redirect Git repository metadata to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the intended clone destination. This can lead to arbitrary directory and file creation bounded only by process permissions. When combined with subsequent Git operations that trigger hook execution on the redirected repository, this vulnerability can escalate to arbitrary code execution. Exploitation requires that the application passes untrusted, attacker-controlled input to the `separate_git_dir` keyword argument of `Repo.clone_from()` or `Repo.clone()` methods without proper validation, while the `allow_unsafe_options` parameter remains at its default value of False.

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity flaw was found in ModelScope, a Python library included as a dependency in the KServe components of Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI). ModelScope parses model configuration files using PyYAML's unsafe yaml.Loader, which permits Python object construction tags in the YAML input to instantiate arbitrary objects. A remote attacker can craft a malicious model repository containing poisoned configuration files; when a user loads such a configuration, the attacker-supplied code executes in the context of the user's process, resulting in arbitrary code execution with high impact to confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Red Hat rates this flaw as IMPORTANT with a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream assessment; exploitation requires a user to load an attacker-supplied configuration file. The affected Red Hat OpenShift AI components are delegated to the RHOAI engineering team, whose analysis determined that the vulnerable code is not in the execute path of the shipped components, so it is not reachable through supported Red Hat OpenShift AI usage.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fastify. An unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass request validation by exploiting how fastify processes boolean false schemas. This could result in unauthorized operations or state changes within affected Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, and Red Hat OpenShift Dev Spaces deployments.

Standard TLS connections over TCP, which represent the typical deployment model for the majority of Red Hat workloads and system services, are unaffected.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici's BalancedPool component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate validation. The BalancedPool constructor incorrectly processes its options, silently discarding custom certificate validation functions. Consequently, a peer with an otherwise untrusted certificate may be accepted, potentially compromising the integrity of secure communication.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: TLS certificate validation bypass in BalancedPool via dropped connect options
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw only affects applications that construct an undici BalancedPool with a function-valued connect or tls option — for example, a custom checkServerIdentity callback or connector used for certificate pinning across multiple upstreams. Client, Pool, Agent, and RoundRobinPool destructure these options before the internal JSON-based clone and are not affected. An attacker able to present, on the network path, a TLS endpoint whose certificate the application's custom validator was written to reject — but which still satisfies Node.js's default hostname and chain checks — can have that certificate silently accepted when the connection goes through BalancedPool, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack against affected connections.
This affects undici versions from 7.24.1 up to 7.29.1 and from 8.0.0 up to 8.10.2.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Origin Validation Error

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When the cache or deduplicate interceptor is directly composed onto a Client or Pool, the destination origin is omitted from cache and request-deduplication keys. This allows a remote attacker to perform cross-origin cache poisoning, leading to information disclosure and potentially a full authentication bypass. An attacker could exploit this by having a trusted origin accept a malicious token, without contacting the legitimate trusted origin.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Authentication bypass via cross-origin cache poisoning due to missing origin isolation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is present in the undici HTTP client library used by Node.js. When an application composes undici's Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly onto a Client or Pool object (rather than onto an Agent), the library's internal cache and in-flight-request deduplication keys omit the destination origin. As a result, a cached or in-flight response captured for one upstream origin can be returned for a request intended for a different, trusted origin whenever the method, path, and relevant headers match. In the most severe demonstrated scenario, this allowed an attacker-controlled JWT to be accepted by the application as though it had been validated against a legitimate, trusted issuer, without that issuer ever being contacted — resulting in a full authentication bypass.
Exploitation requires that the affected application attach the Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly to a Client/Pool — the default Agent-based dispatch path is not affected, since Agent already carries the origin in its dispatch options — and that an attacker can influence or collide with the cache/deduplication key for at least one origin the application communicates with.).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Jupyter Server. The server's logging mechanism for HTTP 500 errors fails to properly redact sensitive information. When a request results in an HTTP 500 error and includes a Referer header containing a security token, this token is written to server logs in plaintext. An attacker with access to these logs could retrieve the token, potentially gaining unauthorized access to the affected user's Jupyter Server permissions.

notes.text: jupyter-server: Jupyter Server: Information disclosure via 5xx request logging

Consequently, while authentication tokens present in request headers can be recorded without proper sanitization during server faults, unauthorized third parties cannot capture these credentials remotely without preexisting elevated privileges.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the GridFS component of the MongoDB Python Driver (pymongo). The driver can treat a caller-supplied structured file identifier as a MongoDB query condition instead of a literal identifier. An authenticated user who can influence the identifier passed to GridFS download, delete, or rename operations may retrieve stored file content beyond the intended target, delete all GridFS chunks in the affected bucket (rendering stored files unreadable), or rename a file other than the intended target.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pymongo: MongoDB Python Driver: Data disclosure and denial of service via query-operator injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This vulnerability is rated as Important because an authenticated user who can influence a GridFS file identifier can delete all file chunks in the affected bucket, making stored files unreadable, and can retrieve or rename a file other than the intended target. Exploitation requires an application to pass a structured identifier, for example a dictionary containing MongoDB query operators, into GridFS download, delete, or rename APIs rather than a literal identifier such as an ObjectId or string.

pymongo is a client library. A deployment is exploitable only if it calls those GridFS APIs with attacker-influenced identifiers. Scalar identifiers are not interpreted as query conditions. Successful exploitation is limited to GridFS-stored file content. It does not by itself provide code execution or host compromise.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

There is no complete mitigation for applications that must accept untrusted structured GridFS file identifiers. The following measures reduce risk until a patched pymongo is available:

1. Pass only literal identifiers to GridFS download, delete, and rename operations (ObjectId, string, or integer). Do not pass dictionaries, BSON documents, or other structured values derived from user input.
2. Restrict which authenticated users can invoke GridFS operations, and do not expose GridFS APIs to untrusted clients.
3. If GridFS is not required, avoid using the gridfs module.

notes.text:
A flaw was found in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver for version < 1.17.10 and < 2.9.1. 
Improper handling of data query elements in the GridFS component can lead to a file identifier being misinterpreted as a query. An authenticated user can exploit this to delete all GridFS file chunks, making stored file content unreadable, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the MongoDB Go Driver. The GridFS component does not properly sanitize caller-supplied file identifiers before using them in database queries. A structured document passed as a file ID (for example, a BSON document containing query operators) is interpreted as a query condition rather than a literal match value. An authenticated attacker who can influence the file identifier passed to GridFS operations such as Delete, DownloadToStream, or OpenDownloadStream in an affected application can exploit this to delete all chunks in a GridFS bucket, resulting in permanent data loss and denial of service.
The practical impact depends on whether the product's code passes externally-controlled values as GridFS file identifiers.
notes.title: Statement

- Validate file identifiers before passing them to GridFS operations. Ensure that file IDs supplied by users or external systems are scalar values (e.g., primitive.ObjectID or string) and reject any structured BSON documents or maps. This prevents query operator injection.

notes.text: A flaw was found in LiteLLM. Due to a metadata key mismatch in the semantic cache component, an authenticated remote attacker can bypass tenant isolation by submitting semantically similar queries. This issue leads to information disclosure, allowing unauthorized access to cached responses containing other tenants' sensitive data, and may cause connected automated agents to execute unauthorized actions under victim credentials.

notes.text: litellm: LiteLLM: Information disclosure via semantic cache metadata mismatch

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because authenticated multi-tenant users can bypass isolation boundaries to access confidential response data and trigger unauthorized tool execution across distinct accounts. While exploitation requires valid API access to affected proxy routes, the shared caching mechanism compromises confidentiality and integrity across AI workloads. Deployments serving single-tenant workloads or environments where semantic caching is not shared between untrusted tenants face substantially reduced exposure.

notes.text: A flaw was found in vllm-project vLLM. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by manipulating specific arguments within the MoRIIO Acknowledgement Handler component. This manipulation can lead to excessive resource consumption, potentially impacting the availability of the system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: Resource consumption via argument manipulation in MoRIIO Acknowledgement Handler
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of IMPORTANT severity was found in the vLLM MoRIIO KV-transfer connector acknowledgement handling. The functions MoRIIOConnectorScheduler.request_finished, MoRIIOConnectorWorker.get_finished, and MoRIIOWrapper._handle_release_message in vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py allocate resources in response to the request_id and kv_transfer_params arguments without adequate limits. A remote attacker with no privileges or user interaction can manipulate these arguments, for example by sending duplicate release messages for already-terminal transfers, causing unbounded acknowledgement object creation and excessive resource consumption that can deny service to the vLLM inference service. There is no impact on confidentiality or integrity. Red Hat rates this flaw as IMPORTANT (CVSS 3.1: 7.5, AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) because of the high availability impact, whereas the upstream CVE record rates it MODERATE (CVSS 3.1: 5.3) with low availability impact. Red Hat AI Inference Server, Red Hat OpenShift AI, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI offerings that ship vLLM are affected; a fix is being pursued through the responsible engineering teams, and upstream has an open, unmerged pull request addressing the issue.

This can occur in server-side-rendered frameworks when a public page processes a small Buffer.

Exploitation depends on the application serializing Node buffer instances on publicly accessible endpoints, limiting vulnerability exposure strictly to services that handle such data flows.

notes.text: A flaw was found in LightGBM. The software does not properly validate data within text models, which can be exploited by an attacker. By crafting a malicious model file, an attacker can trigger an out-of-bounds write during the SHAP prediction process. This vulnerability could lead to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: LightGBM: LightGBM: Out-of-bounds write via crafted model file
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An out-of-bounds write flaw rated IMPORTANT was found in LightGBM, which is shipped in Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI). LightGBM through 4.7.0 fails to validate child and split array values when parsing text model files. When a crafted model file containing invalid node references is loaded and used for SHAP (feature contribution) prediction, out-of-bounds writes occur at attacker-chosen offsets in the leaf_depth_ buffer, which could lead to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service. Exploitation requires a victim to load and process an attacker-supplied malicious model file; this required user interaction is reflected in the Red Hat CVSS 3.1 score of 7.8, which is lower than the upstream CVSS 4.0 score of 8.5. Within Red Hat OpenShift AI, components that bundle the vulnerable LightGBM library are affected and a fix is being pursued by the responsible business unit. Other RHOAI container images were reviewed and determined not affected because the LightGBM component is not present or the vulnerable code is not in the executed path.

cwe.name: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing

notes.text: A flaw was found in LiteLLM. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to achieve privilege escalation and account takeover by presenting a valid JSON Web Token (JWT) containing an unverified email address that matches an existing user account. Because the authentication process falls back to an email-based lookup without checking if the email is verified, the application associates the attacker's session with the victim's profile. As a result, an attacker can inherit administrative privileges, overwrite account identity bindings, and maintain persistent unauthorized access to administrative endpoints and API keys.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: litellm: LiteLLM: Privilege escalation via unverified email lookup in JWT authentication
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity rather than Moderate because a low-privileged authenticated user can achieve full privilege escalation and administrative takeover across the deployment. In Red Hat OpenShift AI and Ansible Automation Platform environments where LiteLLM integrates with external token issuers, the service omits confirmation of email claim validation during user mapping. An attacker with a valid token containing an unconfirmed target address can seize control of administrative accounts, gaining persistent access to management interfaces and exposed credential stores.

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. notes.text: A flaw was found in Amazon GluonTS, a Python time-series modeling library included in Red Hat OpenShift AI. The model loading component does not safely handle untrusted data during deserialization: when a user or an automated process loads a specially crafted serialized model directory (for example, by calling Predictor.deserialize() on a model directory that is not fully controlled), an attacker can execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the loading process. Red Hat rates this flaw as IMPORTANT (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream CVSS 3.1 assessment; exploitation requires a victim to load a crafted model directory, and execution is confined to the security context of the loading process. Within Red Hat OpenShift AI, this issue affects components that ship the vulnerable gluonts package, and a fix is being pursued through the affected product's update process. OpenShift AI components in which the vulnerable code is not in the execute path have been determined not to be affected.

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw was found in JupyterLab, which Red Hat ships within Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) and Migration Toolkit for Applications offerings. When the useSystemClipboardForCells setting is enabled and pasteCodeCellsWithoutOutput is disabled (the default), the system clipboard cell-paste path accepts attacker-controlled cell JSON without clearing metadata.trusted. A pasted code cell can therefore mark its HTML output as trusted, bypass output sanitization, and execute attacker-supplied script in the authenticated JupyterLab origin as soon as the cell is pasted, without the user executing it. Running in the victim's session, the script can call the Jupyter Server REST API as that user, reading and writing any file under the server root, starting a kernel and running code in it, and opening a terminal where terminals are enabled. A remote attacker needs no JupyterLab account and no access to the server; exploitation requires enticing a user to copy malicious content and paste it into JupyterLab. Markdown and raw cells are not affected because their output is always sanitized. JupyterLab releases prior to 4.5.0, such as those bundled in some Red Hat OpenShift AI images, are not affected because the vulnerable system clipboard paste path was introduced in 4.5.0. notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is bundled in a number of Red Hat offerings, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat OpenShift AI, and other layered products and containers, as well as in Fedora and EPEL community builds. Exploitation requires the prompt value to come from outside the operator's trust boundary: where the operator supplies the prompt directly, they already control the command line, and the effect is corruption of their own environment rather than privilege gain. This is why Red Hat assesses the impact as Moderate, while the upstream project published the advisory with low severity. Fixes for affected Red Hat products and streams are being pursued by the responsible component and product teams under delegated resolution; some community and out-of-support-scope streams will not receive an update.

notes.text: This vulnerability has been rated as Important because an untrusted remote server can remotely terminate an application process through memory exhaustion without requiring credentials. However, systems that explicitly configure CurlAsyncHTTPClient—typically enabled for custom proxy routing or advanced transport options—bypass these protections and do not enforce body size constraints. When such client applications fetch resources from compromised or malicious web endpoints, the resulting decompression bomb can consume all available system memory, leading to an immediate denial of service.

notes.text: A moderate severity vulnerability was found in docling, a document conversion library shipped in Red Hat OpenShift AI and Lightspeed Core offerings. The default docling configuration, which does not enable Tectonic rendering, is not affected. Avoid enabling the Tectonic TikZ engine when processing untrusted LaTeX documents. The default docling configuration does not enable Tectonic rendering and is not affected by this flaw, so deployments that have not opted into LatexBackendOptions(tikz_engine="tectonic") are not exposed. The tikz_engine_allow_shell_escape option, which additionally allows shell command execution through TeX, should not be enabled. For deployments that require Tectonic rendering of untrusted input, no mitigation other than upgrading to a release containing the upstream fix is currently available.

notes.text:
A flaw was found in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver for version < 1.17.10 and < 2.9.1. 
Improper handling of data query elements in the GridFS component can lead to a file identifier being misinterpreted as a query. An authenticated user can exploit this to delete all GridFS file chunks, making stored file content unreadable, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the MongoDB Go Driver. The GridFS component does not properly sanitize caller-supplied file identifiers before using them in database queries. A structured document passed as a file ID (for example, a BSON document containing query operators) is interpreted as a query condition rather than a literal match value. An authenticated attacker who can influence the file identifier passed to GridFS operations such as Delete, DownloadToStream, or OpenDownloadStream in an affected application can exploit this to delete all chunks in a GridFS bucket, resulting in permanent data loss and denial of service.
The practical impact depends on whether the product's code passes externally-controlled values as GridFS file identifiers.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata relevant to your system have been applied.

For details on how to apply this update, refer to:

If upgrading go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver to version 1.17.10 (v1) or 2.9.1 (v2) is not immediately possible, the following steps can reduce exposure:
- Validate file identifiers before passing them to GridFS operations. Ensure that file IDs supplied by users or external systems are scalar values (e.g., primitive.ObjectID or string) and reject any structured BSON documents or maps. This prevents query operator injection.
- Restrict who can supply GridFS file identifiers. Do not allow unauthenticated or low-privilege users to directly control the file ID parameter in GridFS API calls (Delete, OpenDownloadStream, DownloadToStream, etc.).

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go, the Go language implementation of gRPC. This vulnerability, an authorization bypass, is caused by improper input validation of the HTTP/2 `:path` pseudo-header. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending raw HTTP/2 frames with a malformed `:path` that omits the mandatory leading slash. This allows the attacker to bypass defined security policies, potentially leading to unauthorized access to services or information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc/grpc-go: google.golang.org/grpc/authz: gRPC-Go: Authorization bypass due to improper HTTP/2 path validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

To mitigate this issue, implement infrastructure-level normalization to ensure all incoming HTTP/2 `:path` headers are properly formatted with a leading slash before reaching the gRPC-Go server. This can be achieved by configuring a reverse proxy or API gateway to validate and normalize the `:path` header. Ensure that any such intermediary is properly configured and restarted to apply the changes, which may temporarily impact service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Immutable.js, a library providing persistent immutable data structures. This vulnerability occurs when specific List operations, such as List#set or List#setSize, are provided with an index or size value within a particular large range. An attacker could exploit this by providing specially crafted input, leading to an uncatchable infinite loop or unbounded memory allocation, ultimately causing a Denial of Service (DoS) for applications using the library.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: immutable-js: Immutable.js: Denial of Service due to mishandling of large index values in List operations
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate impact denial of service vulnerability in Immutable.js affects Red Hat products that process untrusted input through List operations. An attacker can trigger an infinite loop or unbounded memory allocation by providing specially crafted large index values, leading to a service disruption. Additionally, silent data corruption may occur due to integer wrapping.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

To mitigate this issue, applications should implement input validation to reject or clamp any externally supplied List index or key-path segment that exceeds a sane maximum, specifically values greater than or equal to 2^30. Additionally, running request handling in isolated worker processes with capped heap sizes (e.g., using `--max-old-space-size`) can contain the impact of a potential process abort.

notes.text: A flaw was found in proxy-addr. When an application defines trusted proxy subnets using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses with an improper prefix length, the subnet parser fails open and erroneously treats all incoming network addresses as trusted. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a forged X-Forwarded-For header to spoof their client IP address. This flaw allows attackers to bypass IP-based access controls, rate limiting, and audit logging.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: proxy-addr: proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because unauthenticated remote attackers can spoof client IP addresses and circumvent security controls, such as rate limits or network access lists, by sending custom forwarding headers. Exploitation is contingent on application configurations that define reverse proxy trust subnets using IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation with short IPv4 prefix lengths. Environments configuring trusted proxies via canonical IPv4 CIDR blocks, hostnames, or default loopback addresses are not vulnerable to this behavior.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

To mitigate this flaw through configuration:

1. Configure trusted proxy definitions using standard IPv4 notation (such as `10.0.0.0/8`) rather than IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation.
2. If IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation is required, set the subnet prefix length to at least 97 to cover the mapped boundary (for example, specify `::ffff:10.0.0.0/104` instead of `::ffff:10.0.0.0/8`).
3. Alternatively, sanitize or strip incoming `X-Forwarded-For` headers at edge load balancers or boundary reverse proxies before passing traffic to backend applications.

Warning: Modifying application configuration files requires restarting the Node.js application service, which will temporarily interrupt service availability and active connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in joi. A remote attacker can exploit an unanchored regular expression in the `Joi.string().isoDate()` validation rule by supplying a specially crafted string. This vulnerability leads to a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS), allowing the attacker to stall the application with a single request.

This can significantly impact the availability of services utilizing the vulnerable `joi` versions for ISO date validation.

notes.text: A flaw was found in nanoid (Nano ID), a small, secure, and URL-friendly unique string ID generator. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a zero-size input to the customAlphabet or customRandom functions. This would cause an infinite loop, leading to a denial of service (DoS) condition by hanging the application's calling thread.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: nanoid: nanoid: Denial of Service via infinite loop in random ID generation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An algorithmic denial of service flaw was found in the `nanoid` library. When calling `customAlphabet` or `customRandom` with a `size` parameter of `0`, the internal generation loop fails to meet its termination condition. In Node.js or browser execution contexts, an attacker who supplies an unvalidated, zero-value size parameter to these functions causes the thread to enter an infinite loop, driving CPU utilization to 100% and completely blocking event loop execution for that thread.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in nanoid (Nano ID), a JavaScript library used for generating unique identifiers. This vulnerability allows an attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by providing a negative size input to the customAlphabet or nanoid functions within the library's non-secure module. When a negative size is provided, these functions enter an infinite loop, causing the application to hang indefinitely and disrupting service availability.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: nanoid: nanoid: Denial of Service via negative size input in non-secure module functions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An input validation flaw in Nano ID's non-secure module (`nanoid/non-secure`) causes an infinite loop in the `customAlphabet` and `nanoid` functions when processed with a negative size parameter. Because the decrementing loop counter never meets its termination condition, an unauthenticated attacker who passes an unvalidated negative integer value can block the NodeJS event loop, resulting in a thread hang and complete Denial of Service (DoS) for the host application.

notes.text: A flaw was found in etcd, a distributed key-value store. A remote attacker can exploit this by opening numerous TCP connections to an etcd TLS listener without completing the TLS handshake. This action causes the `tlsListener.acceptLoop` to spawn an unbounded number of goroutines, which consume excessive memory. This resource exhaustion leads to a Denial of Service (DoS) for the etcd cluster and, consequently, for the Kubernetes control plane it supports.

cwe.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

notes.text: A flaw was found in go-git, an extensible Git implementation library. Worktree operations, such as checkout, status, and add, resolve symbolic links within the working tree without proper boundary confinement. This allows a remote attacker to craft a malicious repository containing a symlink, which, when cloned and its worktree operations are used, can lead to reading from or writing to arbitrary files outside the intended working directory. This could result in information disclosure or arbitrary file modification.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/go-git/go-git/v5: go-git: Arbitrary file read/write via symbolic link resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: go-git is a pure-Go implementation of Git. During worktree operations (checkout, status, add), go-git resolves symbolic links without confining resolution to the worktree boundary, so a maliciously crafted repository containing a symlink can cause a consuming application to read from or write to files outside the intended working directory when that repository is cloned and its worktree operations are used. Exploitation requires the application to clone an attacker-controlled repository and then perform worktree operations against it; applications that only process trusted repositories are not exposed. Red Hat rates the impact of this flaw as Important.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in etcd, a distributed key-value store. A remote attacker can exploit this by opening numerous TCP connections to an etcd TLS listener without completing the TLS handshake. This action causes the `tlsListener.acceptLoop` to spawn an unbounded number of goroutines, which consume excessive memory. This resource exhaustion leads to a Denial of Service (DoS) for the etcd cluster and, consequently, for the Kubernetes control plane it supports.

notes.text: A flaw was found in aws-smithy-json. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) in smithy-rs generated servers. By sending a small HTTP request containing deeply nested JSON, the attacker can trigger uncontrolled recursion in the aws-smithy-json runtime, leading to stack exhaustion and a process abort. This can make the affected server unavailable to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: aws-smithy-json: aws-smithy-json: Denial of Service via uncontrolled recursion with deeply nested JSON
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw in the `aws-smithy-json` runtime crate allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to trigger a denial of service by sending a crafted HTTP request with deeply nested JSON. Red Hat products utilizing `smithy-rs` generated servers, such as components in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Red Hat Trusted Artifact Signer, are susceptible to service disruption if exposed to untrusted networks.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/html. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted HTML. When this arbitrary HTML is parsed and rendered, it can result in an unexpected HTML tree, bypassing input sanitization. This can be leveraged to execute Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution in applications that use the affected component.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/html: golang.org/x/net/html: Arbitrary code execution via Cross-Site Scripting
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important vulnerability in `golang.org/x/net/html` could enable remote attackers to execute Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution. The flaw allows specially crafted HTML to bypass input sanitization during parsing and rendering. Red Hat products are affected if they process untrusted HTML content using the vulnerable component without additional output encoding or robust content security policies.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/html. When arbitrary HTML is parsed and then rendered, it can result in an unexpected HTML tree. This allows an attacker to bypass HTML sanitization mechanisms, leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks in applications. Such attacks can result in information disclosure or arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/html: golang: golang.org/x/net/html: Cross-Site Scripting via HTML parsing bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability in `golang.org/x/net/html` is rated as Important. It allows for Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks by enabling an attacker to bypass HTML sanitization mechanisms when arbitrary HTML is parsed and rendered. This can lead to information disclosure or arbitrary code execution in affected applications. Exploitation typically requires user interaction, where a user processes specially crafted malicious HTML content.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenTelemetry-Go, the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple 'baggage' header lines. The system's independent parsing and aggregation of each header field-value across multiple values can lead to amplified CPU and memory allocations, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go: OpenTelemetry-Go: Denial of Service via crafted multi-value baggage headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in OpenTelemetry-Go, affecting Red Hat Multicluster Engine for Kubernetes. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by sending multiple crafted `baggage` HTTP header lines, leading to excessive CPU and memory consumption and potentially rendering services unavailable. This impact is significant due to the potential for widespread disruption in a multi-cluster environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple key update messages in a single record after the handshake. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Go crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple TLS 1.3 key update messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: A flaw in the Go `crypto/tls` package allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service in applications using TLS 1.3. By sending multiple key update messages in a single record post-handshake, an attacker can trigger a connection deadlock, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption. This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in github.com/buger/jsonparser. The Delete function, when processing malformed JSON input, fails to properly validate offsets. This vulnerability can lead to a negative slice index and a runtime panic, allowing a remote attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) by providing specially crafted JSON data.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go, the Go language implementation of gRPC. This vulnerability, an authorization bypass, is caused by improper input validation of the HTTP/2 `:path` pseudo-header. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending raw HTTP/2 frames with a malformed `:path` that omits the mandatory leading slash. This allows the attacker to bypass defined security policies, potentially leading to unauthorized access to services or information disclosure.

remediations.details: To mitigate this issue, implement infrastructure-level normalization to ensure all incoming HTTP/2 `:path` headers are properly formatted with a leading slash before reaching the gRPC-Go server. This can be achieved by configuring a reverse proxy or API gateway to validate and normalize the `:path` header. Ensure that any such intermediary is properly configured and restarted to apply the changes, which may temporarily impact service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the SPDY streaming code used by Kubelet, CRI-O, and kube-apiserver. An attacker with specific cluster roles, such as those allowing access to pod port forwarding, execution, or attachment, or node proxying, could exploit this vulnerability. This could lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by causing the affected components to become unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: Kubelet: CRI-O: kube-apiserver: Kubelet, CRI-O, kube-apiserver: Denial of Service via SPDY streaming code
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw affecting OpenShift Container Platform. An attacker with specific elevated cluster roles, such as those permitting pod port forwarding, execution, attachment, or node proxying, could exploit a vulnerability in the SPDY streaming code of Kubelet, CRI-O, and kube-apiserver, leading to unresponsiveness of these critical components.

remediations.details: To mitigate this issue, review and restrict the assignment of Kubernetes cluster roles `pods/portforward (create)`, `pods/exec (create)`, `pods/attach (create)`, and `nodes/proxy (get/create)` to untrusted users or service accounts. Ensure that only authorized and necessary entities possess these permissions. Modifying RBAC policies can impact the functionality of applications and services that rely on these permissions; careful testing is recommended.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenTelemetry-Go. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or invalid baggage headers. The `Parse` function, in affected versions, failed to reject raw-length inputs, leading to excessive processing and error logging when handling these large inputs.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation: OpenTelemetry-Go: Denial of Service via oversized baggage headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in OpenTelemetry-Go, affecting versions 1.41.0 and 1.43.0. An attacker can exploit this flaw by sending oversized baggage headers, causing the `Parse` function to process invalid inputs and log errors, which can lead to resource exhaustion and service disruption in Red Hat products utilizing these affected OpenTelemetry-Go versions. The impact is considered Important due to the potential for remote, unauthenticated denial of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Prometheus, an open-source monitoring system. The `client_secret` field within the Azure Active Directory (AD) remote write OAuth configuration was incorrectly handled as a plain string instead of a secure Secret type. This misconfiguration allowed any user or process with access to the `/-/config` HTTP API endpoint to view the Azure OAuth client secret in plaintext. This vulnerability leads to information disclosure, potentially compromising the security of integrated Azure AD services.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/prometheus/prometheus: Prometheus: Information disclosure of Azure OAuth client secret via config API
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important information disclosure flaw in Prometheus affects instances configured to use Azure AD remote write with OAuth authentication. The client secret, intended to be a secure credential, is exposed in plaintext through the `/-/config` HTTP API endpoint. This could allow an attacker with access to this endpoint to retrieve the secret, potentially compromising integrated Azure AD services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Prometheus. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit the remote read endpoint (`/api/v1/read`) by sending a specially crafted, small snappy-compressed payload. This payload causes a disproportionately large memory allocation, leading to memory exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the Prometheus process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/prometheus/prometheus: Prometheus: Denial of Service via uncontrolled memory allocation in remote read endpoint
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in Prometheus, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to crash the Prometheus process. This could lead to service unavailability in Red Hat products that deploy Prometheus for monitoring, as the remote read endpoint does not properly validate snappy-compressed request lengths.

Configure firewall rules or network policies to permit connections only from trusted internal networks or authorized clients. This action reduces the attack surface by limiting exposure to unauthenticated remote attackers. A service restart or reload may be required for the changes to take effect.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/mail` package within the Go standard library. A remote attacker could provide specially crafted, pathological email addresses. When these malformed email addresses are parsed by the `consumePhrase` function, it can lead to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic string concatenation, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/mail: golang: net/mail: Denial of Service via pathological email address parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `net/mail` package of the Go standard library. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by sending specially crafted email addresses, leading to excessive resource consumption and a denial of service in Go applications that parse email addresses using the affected library.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/html. This vulnerability allows an attacker to manipulate how HTML is processed and displayed. By providing specially crafted HTML, an attacker can cause an unexpected structure in the rendered output. This can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, where malicious scripts are executed in a user's web browser, potentially compromising user data or taking control of their session.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/html: golang: golang.org/x/net/html: Cross-Site Scripting via unexpected HTML tree rendering
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw in golang.org/x/net/html can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in applications that parse and render untrusted HTML, even with sanitization attempts. This is due to an unexpected HTML tree structure, allowing malicious scripts to execute in a user's browser.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage. A remote attacker could send a specially crafted Service Binding (SVCB) or HTTPS resource record (RR) to a system using this component. When parsing this invalid record, the system may panic due to a parameter value overflowing the message buffer. This can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition, making the affected system unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/text. The norm.Iter component can enter an infinite loop when processing input that contains invalid UTF-8 (Unicode Transformation Format - 8-bit) bytes. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted input, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition where the affected application becomes unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/text: golang.org/x/text: Denial of Service via invalid UTF-8 input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: This flaw in the `golang.org/x/text` library can lead to a denial of service. An attacker could provide specially crafted invalid UTF-8 input to an application using the affected `norm.Iter` functionality, causing it to enter an infinite loop and become unresponsive.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/xml` package of Go. The `DecodeElement` function failed to correctly track recursion depth, which could lead to stack exhaustion. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML input, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important denial of service flaw affects applications utilizing the Go `encoding/xml` package. This vulnerability arises from an issue in XML decoding where a recursion depth counter fails to reset, potentially leading to stack exhaustion when processing malicious XML input.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost/compress package. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted compression dictionary with an excessively large repeat value, triggering an integer overflow. When the dictionary is subsequently processed, this overflow leads to out-of-bounds memory access, crashing the application and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via integer overflow in dictionary processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as having an impact of Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker could trigger a denial of service by causing a process crash without requiring elevated permissions. In Red Hat environments where this Go library is embedded, exploitation requires that an application accepts untrusted dictionary structures for S2 compression and subsequently attempts encoding. Although the resulting memory access fault terminates the vulnerable process, the flaw is confined to process crashes and does not compromise data confidentiality or integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.

cwe.name: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. This vulnerability allows for cross-user information disclosure when malformed Cache-Control private directives cause private response bodies and headers, such as Set-Cookie data, to be stored in a shared cache and subsequently exposed to other users. Additionally, a specially crafted Cache-Control header can trigger an unhandled error in the cache parser, leading to a process termination and a Denial of Service (DoS). Both issues affect applications using the cache interceptor in shared mode.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending a large number of QUIC Initial packets to an OpenSSL QUIC server. This can cause the server to allocate and queue new incoming channels without limit, leading to unbounded memory growth. The excessive memory consumption can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) condition, making the QUIC listener unavailable.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via unbounded memory growth in QUIC server
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8+, 10.2+, Red Hat Hardened Images, RHIVOS 2, and OpenShift 4.22 ship OpenSSL 3.5.x which includes the QUIC server implementation affected by this flaw. Earlier RHEL versions ship OpenSSL 3.2.x or below, which do not include the QUIC server feature and are not affected. The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary. Applications must explicitly enable the QUIC server listener to be vulnerable; simply having OpenSSL 3.5 installed does not expose the flaw.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more about Red Hat Developer Hub, see References links

Option 1: Rate-limit or Firewall Inbound QUIC (UDP 443) [Goal: Slow or block QUIC Initial packets before they reach the vulnerable listener.]

A. Confirm QUIC Exposure - Check if any service is listening on UDP 443:
~~~
$ ss -ulnp | grep ':443'
# or
$ sudo lsof -iUDP:443 -n -P
~~~

Note: If no service is listening on UDP 443, this CVE does not apply (TCP 443 is unaffected).

B. Restrict Access to UDP 443 ( Default-deny UDP 443 and allow only trusted networks:)
~~~
$ sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-service=quic 2>/dev/null
$ sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="10.0.0.0/8" port port="443" protocol="udp" accept'
$ sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" port port="443" protocol="udp" drop'
$ sudo firewall-cmd --reload
~~~

C. Verify - Confirm the restriction by testing from an external host (the connection should fail or be throttled):
~~~
$ nc -u -v YOUR_HOST 443
~~~

Option 2: Disable QUIC Server

If QUIC/HTTP3 is not required, remove the vulnerable code path entirely and use TLS/TCP instead.

Recommended Mitigation Priority
Priority : Action
1.Confirm UDP 443 QUIC listener exists and OpenSSL version is in affected range
2.Block or rate-limit UDP 443 at firewall/edge (immediate)
3.Disable QUIC/HTTP3 on the service if not needed
4.Upgrade OpenSSL to fixed release when available
5.Application owners: set SSL_VALUE_QUIC_MAX_PENDING_CONNS if default 256 is too high

cwe.name: Double Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL. A malformed INITIAL packet with an invalid DCID (destination connection ID) can cause the QUIC server to double free the QRX object. This issue leads to memory corruption, causing the termination of the QUIC server process and resulting in a denial of service.

notes.text: openssl: QUIC server may trigger double free when processing INITIAL packet
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue can cause memory corruption due to the double free of the QRX object. However, there is currently no evidence it allows remote code execution, limiting the impact of this vulnerability to a denial of service. For these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by responding with an unrequested WebSocket subprotocol during the opening handshake. This causes the undici WebSocket client to crash the entire Node.js process, leading to a denial of service (DoS).

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in vm2, an open-source virtual machine (VM) sandbox for Node.js. This vulnerability allows malicious code running within the sandbox to bypass the configured memory allocation limit. By crafting specific calls to Buffer.concat or Buffer.from with attacker-controlled lengths, the sandbox code can perform large, synchronous memory allocations on the host system. This can exhaust the host process's memory, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important vulnerability in the vm2 sandbox library allows malicious code to bypass memory allocation limits, leading to host process exhaustion and a Denial of Service. This is particularly relevant for Red Hat products like Ansible Automation Platform and Red Hat Developer Hub that utilize vm2 for executing untrusted Node.js code, as it can compromise the availability of the host system.

cwe.name: Protection Mechanism Failure

notes.text: A flaw was found in vm2. The sandbox fails to properly sanitize the error cause property when handling exceptions thrown by host functions. An attacker capable of running untrusted code within the sandbox can exploit this issue to access privileged host objects and bypass isolation boundaries. Consequently, this flaw allows the attacker to escape the sandbox and achieve arbitrary code execution on the underlying host system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vm2: vm2: Missing Error.cause Sanitization Enables VM2 Sandbox Escape to RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact for Red Hat products because an attacker capable of executing untrusted scripts within the sandbox environment can escape isolation and execute arbitrary commands in the host process. Successful exploitation requires specific preconditions, namely that an embedder-provided host function exposes chained error objects referencing privileged runtime structures. Consequently, the blast radius allows full host process compromise, though execution depends on the presence and invocation of these specific host error paths.

cwe.name: Improper Control of Dynamically-Managed Code Resources

notes.text: A flaw was found in vm2. This vulnerability allows arbitrary code execution on the host system through a sandbox breakout. An attacker capable of running code inside the sandbox can manipulate host object properties using indirect function calls to bypass isolation boundaries and execute arbitrary commands directly on the host.

notes.text: vm2: vm2: Sandbox Breakout Using Dangerous Host Proto Mutators
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL. A crafted CMS (Cryptographic Message Syntax) message can cause an 8-byte out-of-bounds heap write when it is decrypted with CMS_decrypt(). This issue occurs because the CMS decryption process incorrectly sizes the key-unwrap output buffer when using the AES-WRAP-PAD unwrap primitive. For these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in nanoid (Nano ID), a small, secure, and URL-friendly unique string ID generator. notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. Its custom parser for bracketed IPv6 literals does not fully validate the IPv6 grammar, allowing invalid trailing text in an authority to be silently discarded. This can lead to a malformed, attacker-controlled host being normalized into a different, valid IPv6 destination, such as a local or private IPv6 target. An application normalizing untrusted URLs before outbound requests, redirects, or proxy routing could be redirected, resulting in a server-side request forgery (SSRF) and address-policy bypass.

The parser's incomplete validation of bracketed IPv6 literals allows attackers to inject malformed authority components that are silently normalized to different valid IPv6 destinations. This could allow an attacker to bypass URL allowlists or network-based access controls, potentially enabling unauthorized access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or other network resources. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Equivalent Special Elements

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a software component used for parsing Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) in Node.js applications. This vulnerability arises from an issue in how fast-uri processes the scheme part of a URI, specifically when it contains special characters that are percent-encoded. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious URI, causing the parser to misinterpret the host, which can lead to serious security risks. These risks include unauthorized redirection to external websites, server-side request forgery (SSRF) where the application makes unintended requests to internal or external resources, and bypassing security policies.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: URI parsing flaw enables server-side request forgery and redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A host confusion vulnerability was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. The parser runs a legacy decoding pass over the scheme component and never re-escapes the result. As a consequence, an input whose scheme carries percent-encoded slashes parses as having no authority (undefined host), yet resolving or normalizing that same input emits a network-path reference with an attacker-chosen authority. Applications that normalize or resolve untrusted URLs before a redirect check, host allowlist, or outbound request decision can be steered to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF), open redirect, or address-policy bypass. Additionally, a normalized URI in a response header can carry injected carriage return line feed (CRLF) characters, enabling HTTP response splitting attacks such as cache poisoning or session hijacking. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in multer, a Node.js middleware for handling multipart/form-data. A remote attacker can exploit a file descriptor leak by sending repeated aborted or malformed multipart uploads. This can exhaust system resources, leading to a denial of service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: multer: Multer: Denial of Service via file descriptor leak on aborted uploads
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A file descriptor leak vulnerability was found in multer, a Node.js middleware for handling multipart/form-data. When using multer's built-in diskStorage engine, aborted or truncated uploads cause the disk storage engine to remove the visible file but fail to close the underlying write file descriptor. A remote attacker able to reach an upload route can send repeated aborted or malformed multipart uploads, each one leaking a file descriptor and retaining disk blocks until the process exits, which can exhaust system resources and cause a denial of service. This vulnerability only affects applications using multer's diskStorage; applications using memoryStorage or custom storage engines are not affected.

notes.text: Multiple vulnerabilities were found in multer, a Node.js middleware for handling multipart/form-data. notes.text: A flaw was found in qs. The `qs.stringify` function, responsible for serializing objects, does not properly validate the `isBuffer` property of an object's constructor before attempting to invoke it. An unauthenticated attacker can provide specially crafted input that, when processed and then serialized by `qs.stringify`, triggers a `TypeError`. This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS), causing affected applications to return a 500 error or, in certain scenarios, terminate the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: qs: qs: Denial of Service via improper validation in stringify function
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A denial of service vulnerability was found in the qs package for Node.js. The stringify function does not verify that constructor.isBuffer is callable before invoking it. An attacker who can influence object shape, for example through query parameters parsed with allowPrototypes: true as Express 4 does by default, can cause qs.stringify to throw a TypeError when that data is re-serialized. In typical Node.js HTTP frameworks the error is caught per request and returns HTTP 500. In code paths without an error boundary, such as async handlers or background jobs, the process may exit.

Wrapping qs.stringify calls in try/catch can limit impact to individual requests.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici's BalancedPool component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate validation. The BalancedPool constructor incorrectly processes its options, silently discarding custom certificate validation functions. Consequently, a peer with an otherwise untrusted certificate may be accepted, potentially compromising the integrity of secure communication.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: TLS certificate validation bypass in BalancedPool via dropped connect options
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw only affects applications that construct an undici BalancedPool with a function-valued connect or tls option — for example, a custom checkServerIdentity callback or connector used for certificate pinning across multiple upstreams. Client, Pool, Agent, and RoundRobinPool destructure these options before the internal JSON-based clone and are not affected. An attacker able to present, on the network path, a TLS endpoint whose certificate the application's custom validator was written to reject — but which still satisfies Node.js's default hostname and chain checks — can have that certificate silently accepted when the connection goes through BalancedPool, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack against affected connections.
This affects undici versions from 7.24.1 up to 7.29.1 and from 8.0.0 up to 8.10.2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more about Red Hat Developer Hub, see References links

Applications that do not use BalancedPool, or that use it without a custom function-valued connect/tls option, are not affected and require no action. As a workaround until packages are updated, avoid using BalancedPool for any connection that relies on custom TLS certificate validation (e.g. certificate pinning); use Client, Pool, or Agent instead, which are unaffected. The permanent fix is upgrading undici to 7.29.1 or later (7.x line) or 8.10.2 or later (8.x line).

cwe.name: Incomplete Cleanup

notes.text: A flaw was found in multer, a Node.js middleware for handling multipart/form-data uploads. When a request using disk storage is aborted during an upload, file writes that complete after multer's cleanup process are not removed. This can leave orphaned files on disk. A remote unauthenticated attacker can repeatedly initiate and abort uploads to accumulate these orphaned files, which can exhaust disk space and lead to a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: multer: multer: Denial of Service via orphaned disk writes on aborted uploads
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate flaw in `multer` can lead to a denial of service in Red Hat products that process multipart/form-data uploads. A remote unauthenticated attacker can repeatedly initiate and abort uploads, causing orphaned files to accumulate and exhaust available disk space. This risk is present in deployments where `multer` is configured for disk storage.
